It involves prompting an LLM to reflect on and critique its past actions, sometimes incorporating additional external information such as tool observations. </p><p>People like to talk about "System 1" and "System 2" thinking, where System 1 is reactive or instinctive and System 2 is more methodical and reflective. When applied correctly, reflection can help LLM systems break out of purely System 1 "thinking" patterns and closer to something exhibiting System 2-like behavior.</p><figure style="max-width:1125pxpx" class="w-richtext-align-fullwidth w-richtext-figure-type-image"><div style="width: 100% !important; max-width: 100% !important;"><img loading="eager" alt="System 1 and 2: Thinking fast? Slow down." src="https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65c81e88c254bb0f97633a71/69cbb0172c87c962360c6c88_System-12-White-1.png" style="cursor: zoom-in;"></div></figure><p>Reflection takes time! All the approaches in this post trade off a bit of extra compute for a shot at better output quality. While this may not be appropriate for low-latency applications, it <em>is</em> worthwhile for knowledge intensive tasks where response <em>quality</em> is more important than speed.</p><p>The three examples are outlined below:</p></div><div id="basic-reflection" style="scroll-margin-top: 8rem;"><h2>Basic Reflection</h2><p><strong>Links: (</strong><a href="https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/main/examples/reflection/reflection.ipynb?ref=blog.langchain.com" data-wf-native-id-path="ee7399a4-616a-66fe-d099-19f596572429" data-wf-ao-click-engagement-tracking="true" data-wf-element-id="ee7399a4-616a-66fe-d099-19f596572429"><strong>Python</strong></a><strong>, </strong><a href="https://youtu.be/v5ymBTXNqtk?feature=shared&t=48&ref=blog.langchain.com" data-wf-native-id-path="3f033fa3-359a-5143-5ee2-61e82996a1e3" data-wf-ao-click-engagement-tracking="true" data-wf-element-id="3f033fa3-359a-5143-5ee2-61e82996a1e3"><strong>Youtube</strong></a><strong>)</strong></p><p>This simple example composes two LLM calls: a generator and a reflector. The generator tries to respond directly to the user's requests. The reflector is prompted to role play as a teacher  and offer constructive criticism for the initial response.</p><p>The loop proceeds a fixed number of times, and the final generated output is returned. </p><figure style="max-width:2000pxpx" class="w-richtext-align-fullwidth w-richtext-figure-type-image"><div style="width: 100% !important; max-width: 100% !important;"><img loading="eager" alt="" src="https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65c81e88c254bb0f97633a71/69cbb0172c87c962360c6c71_reflection.png" style="cursor: zoom-in;"></div><figcaption>Simple Reflection Loop</figcaption></figure><p>We can define the loop in LangGraph below:</p><div class="code-wrapper"><div class="code-actions"><button class="code-action-btn code-copy-btn" title="Copy"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="5" y="5" width="9" height="10" rx="1.5"></rect><path d="M11 5V3.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 9.5 2h-7A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 1 3.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 2.5 13H5"></path></svg></button><button class="code-action-btn code-expand-btn" title="Expand"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M10 2h4v4M6 14H2v-4M14 2l-5 5M2 14l5-5"></path></svg></button></div><div class="code-body"><div class="code-content"><pre><code class="language-bash hljs" data-highlighted="yes"><span class="code-line">from langgraph.graph import MessageGraph</span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line">builder = MessageGraph()</span>
<span class="code-line">builder.add_node(<span class="hljs-string">"generate"</span>, generation_node)</span>
<span class="code-line">builder.add_node(<span class="hljs-string">"reflect"</span>, reflection_node)</span>
<span class="code-line">builder.set_entry_point(<span class="hljs-string">"generate"</span>)</span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line">def should_continue(state: List[BaseMessage]):</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> len(state) > 6:</span>
<span class="code-line">        <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span> END</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span> <span class="hljs-string">"reflect"</span></span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line">builder.add_conditional_edges(<span class="hljs-string">"generate"</span>, should_continue)</span>
<span class="code-line">builder.add_edge(<span class="hljs-string">"reflect"</span>, <span class="hljs-string">"generate"</span>)</span>
<span class="code-line">graph = builder.compile()</span></code></pre></div></div></div><p>The <code>MessageGraph</code> represents a stateful graph, where the "state" is simply a list of messages. Each time the generator or reflector node is called, it appends a message to the end of the state. The final result is returned from the generator node.</p><p>This simple type of reflection can sometimes improve performance by giving the LLM multiple attempts at refining its output and by letting the reflection node adopt a different persona while critiquing the output.</p><p>However, since the reflection step isn't grounded in any external process, the final result may not be significantly better than the original. Let's explore some other techniques that can ameliorate that.</p></div><div id="reflexion" style="scroll-margin-top: 8rem;"><h2>Reflexion</h2><p><strong>Links: (</strong><a href="https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/main/examples/reflexion/reflexion.ipynb?ref=blog.langchain.com" data-wf-native-id-path="1e9eae1a-d5b3-70a4-a4bf-9023f1c9025f" data-wf-ao-click-engagement-tracking="true" data-wf-element-id="1e9eae1a-d5b3-70a4-a4bf-9023f1c9025f"><strong>Python</strong></a><strong>, </strong><a href="https://youtu.be/v5ymBTXNqtk?feature=shared&t=299&ref=blog.langchain.com" data-wf-native-id-path="bc83264b-fea7-df1c-3d6f-e8e426d092ca" data-wf-ao-click-engagement-tracking="true" data-wf-element-id="bc83264b-fea7-df1c-3d6f-e8e426d092ca"><strong>Youtube</strong></a><strong>)</strong></p><p><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366?ref=blog.langchain.com" data-wf-native-id-path="acf117b1-ad8b-d77a-d756-c3340e54d92f" data-wf-ao-click-engagement-tracking="true" data-wf-element-id="acf117b1-ad8b-d77a-d756-c3340e54d92f">Reflexion</a> by Shinn, et. al., is an architecture designed to learn through verbal feedback and self-reflection. Within reflexion, the <em>actor</em> agent explicitly critiques each response and grounds its criticism in external data. It is forced to generate citations and explicitly enumerate superfluous and missing aspects of the generated response. This makes the content of the reflections more constructive and better steers the generator in responding to the feedback.</p><p>In the <a href="https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/main/examples/reflexion/reflexion.ipynb?ref=blog.langchain.com" data-wf-native-id-path="88823e89-87f0-40d2-2309-6ef1ed3f749f" data-wf-ao-click-engagement-tracking="true" data-wf-element-id="88823e89-87f0-40d2-2309-6ef1ed3f749f">linked</a> example, we stop after a fixed number of steps, though you can also offload this decision to the reflection LLM call.</p><p>An overview of the agent loop is shown below:</p><figure style="max-width:2000pxpx" class="w-richtext-align-fullwidth w-richtext-figure-type-image"><div style="width: 100% !important; max-width: 100% !important;"><img loading="eager" alt="" src="https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65c81e88c254bb0f97633a71/69cbb0172c87c962360c6c74_reflexion.png" style="cursor: zoom-in;"></div><figcaption>Reflexion Actor Overview</figcaption></figure><p>For each step, the responder is tasked with generating a response, along with additional actions in the form of search queries. Then the revisor is prompted to reflect on the current state. The logic can be defined in LangGraph as follows:</p><div class="code-wrapper"><div class="code-actions"><button class="code-action-btn code-copy-btn" title="Copy"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="5" y="5" width="9" height="10" rx="1.5"></rect><path d="M11 5V3.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 9.5 2h-7A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 1 3.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 2.5 13H5"></path></svg></button><button class="code-action-btn code-expand-btn" title="Expand"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M10 2h4v4M6 14H2v-4M14 2l-5 5M2 14l5-5"></path></svg></button></div><div class="code-body"><div class="code-content"><pre><code class="language-bash hljs" data-highlighted="yes"><span class="code-line">from langgraph.graph import END, MessageGraph</span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line">MAX_ITERATIONS = 5</span>
<span class="code-line">builder = MessageGraph()</span>
<span class="code-line">builder.add_node(<span class="hljs-string">"draft"</span>, first_responder.respond)</span>
<span class="code-line">builder.add_node(<span class="hljs-string">"execute_tools"</span>, execute_tools)</span>
<span class="code-line">builder.add_node(<span class="hljs-string">"revise"</span>, revisor.respond)</span>
<span class="code-line"><span class="hljs-comment"># draft -> execute_tools</span></span>
<span class="code-line">builder.add_edge(<span class="hljs-string">"draft"</span>, <span class="hljs-string">"execute_tools"</span>)</span>
<span class="code-line"><span class="hljs-comment"># execute_tools -> revise</span></span>
<span class="code-line">builder.add_edge(<span class="hljs-string">"execute_tools"</span>, <span class="hljs-string">"revise"</span>)</span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line"><span class="hljs-comment"># Define looping logic:</span></span>
<span class="code-line">def event_loop(state: List[BaseMessage]) -> str:</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-comment"># in our case, we'll just stop after N plans</span></span>
<span class="code-line">    num_iterations = _get_num_iterations(state)</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> num_iterations > MAX_ITERATIONS:</span>
<span class="code-line">        <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span> END</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span> <span class="hljs-string">"execute_tools"</span></span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line"><span class="hljs-comment"># revise -> execute_tools OR end</span></span>
<span class="code-line">builder.add_conditional_edges(<span class="hljs-string">"revise"</span>, event_loop)</span>
<span class="code-line">builder.set_entry_point(<span class="hljs-string">"draft"</span>)</span>
<span class="code-line">graph = builder.compile()</span></code></pre></div></div></div><p>This agent can effectively use explicit reflections and  web-based citations to improve the quality of the final response. It only pursues one fixed trajectory, however, so if it makes a misstep, that error can impact subsequent decisions.</p></div><div id="language-agent-tree-search" style="scroll-margin-top: 8rem;"><h2>Language Agent Tree Search</h2><p><strong>Links: (</strong><a href="https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/main/examples/lats/lats.ipynb?ref=blog.langchain.com" data-wf-native-id-path="1b8508eb-c915-b698-b3d8-9937ad440a82" data-wf-ao-click-engagement-tracking="true" data-wf-element-id="1b8508eb-c915-b698-b3d8-9937ad440a82"><strong>Python</strong></a><strong>, </strong><a href="https://youtu.be/v5ymBTXNqtk?feature=shared&t=625&ref=blog.langchain.com" data-wf-native-id-path="0d7c7ff9-848c-286f-bd18-9f7723e26210" data-wf-ao-click-engagement-tracking="true" data-wf-element-id="0d7c7ff9-848c-286f-bd18-9f7723e26210"><strong>Youtube</strong></a><strong>)</strong></p><p><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04406?ref=blog.langchain.com" data-wf-native-id-path="cd402926-ef79-6ef9-5464-bc47c395abaa" data-wf-ao-click-engagement-tracking="true" data-wf-element-id="cd402926-ef79-6ef9-5464-bc47c395abaa">Language Agent Tree Search</a> (LATS), by Zhou, et. al, is a general LLM agent search algorithm that combines reflection/evaluation and search (specifically Monte-Carlo trees search) to achieve better overall task performance compared to similar techniques like ReACT, Reflexion, or even Tree of Thoughts. It adopts a standard reinforcement learning (RL) task framing, replacing the RL agents, value functions, and optimizer all with calls to an LLM. This is meant to help the agent adapt and problem solve for complex tasks, avoiding getting stuck in repetitive loops.</p><p>The search process is outlined in the diagram below:</p><figure style="max-width:2000pxpx" class="w-richtext-align-fullwidth w-richtext-figure-type-image"><div style="width: 100% !important; max-width: 100% !important;"><img loading="eager" alt="" src="https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65c81e88c254bb0f97633a71/69cbb0172c87c962360c6c7a_lats.png" style="cursor: zoom-in;"></div></figure><p>The search has four main steps:</p><ol role="list"><li><strong>Select</strong>: pick the best next actions based on the aggregate rewards from step (2) below. Either respond (if a solution is found or the max search depth is reached) or continue searching.</li><li><strong>Expand and simulate:</strong> generate N (5 in our case) potential actions to take and execute them in parallel.</li><li><strong>Reflect + evaluate</strong>: observe the outcomes of these actions and score the decisions based on reflection (and possibly external feedback)</li><li><strong>Backpropagate</strong>: update the scores of the root trajectories based on the outcomes.</li></ol><p>If the agent has a tight feedback loop (through high quality environment rewards or reliable reflection scores), the search is able to accurately distinguish between different action trajectories and pick the best path. The final trajectory can then be saved to external memory (or used for model fine-tuning) to improve the model in the future.</p><p>The "selection" step picks the node with the highest upper confidence bound (UCT), which just balances the expected reward (the first term) with an incentive to explore new paths (the second term).</p><p>\( UCT = \frac{\text{value}}{\text{visits}} + c \sqrt{\frac{\ln(\text{parent.visits})}{\text{visits}}}\)</p><p>Check out the <a href="https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/main/examples/lats/lats.ipynb?ref=blog.langchain.com" data-wf-native-id-path="8fbf8b87-76a7-3924-a7f2-4ee2d00064b5" data-wf-ao-click-engagement-tracking="true" data-wf-element-id="8fbf8b87-76a7-3924-a7f2-4ee2d00064b5">code</a> to see how it's implemented. In our LangGraph implementation, we put generation + reflection steps in a single node each, and check the tree state on each loop to see if the task is solved. The (abbreviated) graph definition looks something like below:</p><div class="code-wrapper"><div class="code-actions"><button class="code-action-btn code-copy-btn" title="Copy"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="5" y="5" width="9" height="10" rx="1.5"></rect><path d="M11 5V3.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 9.5 2h-7A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 1 3.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 2.5 13H5"></path></svg></button><button class="code-action-btn code-expand-btn" title="Expand"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M10 2h4v4M6 14H2v-4M14 2l-5 5M2 14l5-5"></path></svg></button></div><div class="code-body"><div class="code-content"><pre><code class="language-bash hljs" data-highlighted="yes"><span class="code-line">from langgraph.graph import END, StateGraph</span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line">class Node:</span>
<span class="code-line">    def __init__(</span>
<span class="code-line">        self,</span>
<span class="code-line">        messages: List[BaseMessage],</span>
<span class="code-line">        reflection: Reflection,</span>
<span class="code-line">        parent: Optional[Node] = None,</span>
<span class="code-line">    ):</span>
<span class="code-line">        self.messages = messages</span>
<span class="code-line">        self.parent = parent</span>
<span class="code-line">        self.children = []</span>
<span class="code-line">        self.value = 0</span>
<span class="code-line">        self.visits = 0</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-comment"># Additional methods are defined here. Check the code for more!</span></span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line">class TreeState(TypedDict):</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-comment"># The full tree</span></span>
<span class="code-line">    root: Node</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-comment"># The original input</span></span>
<span class="code-line">    input: str</span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line">def should_loop(state: TreeState):</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-string">""</span><span class="hljs-string">"Determine whether to continue the tree search."</span><span class="hljs-string">""</span></span>
<span class="code-line">    root = state[<span class="hljs-string">"root"</span>]</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> root.is_solved:</span>
<span class="code-line">        <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span> END</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> root.height > 5:</span>
<span class="code-line">        <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span> END</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span> <span class="hljs-string">"expand"</span></span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line">builder = StateGraph(TreeState)</span>
<span class="code-line">builder.add_node(<span class="hljs-string">"start"</span>, generate_initial_response)</span>
<span class="code-line">builder.add_node(<span class="hljs-string">"expand"</span>, <span class="hljs-built_in">expand</span>)</span>
<span class="code-line">builder.set_entry_point(<span class="hljs-string">"start"</span>)</span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line">builder.add_conditional_edges(</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-string">"start"</span>,</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-comment"># Either expand/rollout or finish</span></span>
<span class="code-line">    should_loop,</span>
<span class="code-line">)</span>
<span class="code-line">builder.add_conditional_edges(</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-string">"expand"</span>,</span>
<span class="code-line">    <span class="hljs-comment"># Either continue to rollout or finish</span></span>
<span class="code-line">    should_loop,</span>
<span class="code-line">)</span>
<span class="code-line"> </span>
<span class="code-line">graph = builder.compile()</span></code></pre></div></div></div><p>LATS Graph</p><p>Once you've created the basic outline, it's easy to expand to other tasks!  For instance, this technique would suit code generation tasks well, where you the agent can write explicit unit tests and score trajectories based on test quality.</p><p>LATS unifies the reasoning, planning, and reflection  components of other agent architectures, such as Reflexion, Tree of Thoughts, and <a href="https://blog.langchain.com/planning-agents/" data-wf-native-id-path="32772746-319d-7e3f-1e70-5f1a031b1023" data-wf-ao-click-engagement-tracking="true" data-wf-element-id="32772746-319d-7e3f-1e70-5f1a031b1023">plan-and-execute</a> agents. LATS also from the backpropagation of reflective and environment-based feedback for an improved search process. While it can be sensitive to the reward scores, the general algorithm can be flexibly applied to a variety of tasks.</p><figure style="max-width:2000pxpx" class="w-richtext-align-fullwidth w-richtext-figure-type-image"><div style="width: 100% !important; max-width: 100% !important;"><img loading="eager" alt="" src="https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65c81e88c254bb0f97633a71/69cbb0172c87c962360c6c77_image-17.png" style="cursor: zoom-in;"></div><figcaption>Comparison of LATS with other agent architectures</figcaption></figure></div><div id="video-tutorial" style="scroll-margin-top: 8rem;"><h2>Video Tutorial</h2><figure style="padding-bottom:33.75%" class="w-richtext-figure-type-video"><div style="width: 100% !important; max-width: 100% !important;"><iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/v5ymBTXNqtk?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen=""></iframe></div></figure></div><div id="conclusion" style="scroll-margin-top: 8rem;"><h2>Conclusion</h2><p>Thanks for reading!   // Shared animation factory
  function animateLetters(el, { scrollTrigger, delay, colors, durations, stagger }) {
    const { chars } = new SplitType(el, { types: "words, chars" });

    // Set initial state
    if (typeof colors.initial === "function") {
      chars.forEach((char) => {
        const c = colors.initial(char);
        gsap.set(char, { opacity: 0.3, color: c });
      });
    } else {
      gsap.set(chars, { opacity: 0.3, color: colors.initial });
    }

    if (delay !== undefined) gsap.set(el, { opacity: 1 });

    const tl = gsap.timeline(scrollTrigger ? { scrollTrigger } : { delay: delay ?? 0 });

    chars.forEach((char, i) => {
      const highlight = typeof colors.highlight === "function" ? colors.highlight(char) : colors.highlight;
      const base = typeof colors.base === "function" ? colors.base(char) : colors.base;
      const offset = i * stagger;

        opacity: 1,

        ease: durations[2] || undefined,

    function splitHtmlLines(html) {
      var openStack = [];
      var tagRe = /<(\/?)(\w[\w-]*)([^>]*?)(\/?)>/g;
      return html.split('\n').map(function (line) {
        var out = openStack.join('') + line;
        var m;
        tagRe.lastIndex = 0;
        while ((m = tagRe.exec(line)) !== null) {
          var closing = m[1] === '/';
          var selfClose = m[4] === '/';
          var name = m[2];
          var attrs = m[3];
          if (!closing && !selfClose) {
            openStack.push('<' + name + attrs + '>');
          } else if (closing) {
            for (var i = openStack.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
              if (openStack[i].match(new RegExp('^<' + name + '[\\s>]'))) {
                openStack.splice(i, 1);
                break;
              }
            }
          }
        }
        var closeTags = openStack.slice().reverse().map(function (t) {
          return '</' + t.match(/^<(\w[\w-]*)/)[1] + '>';
        }).join('');
        return out + closeTags;
      });
    }

      if (code.closest('.code-wrapper')) return;

        br.replaceWith('\n');
      });
      var rawText = code.textContent.replace(/\n$/, '');
      // Skip inline code that lives alongside other content
      var isInline = Array.from(code.parentNode.childNodes).some(function (node) {
        if (node === code) return false;

      if (isInline) return;
      var detectedLang = code.dataset.lang || (code.className.match(/language-(\w+)/) || [])[1];
      var lang = detectedLang || 'bash';
      if (!detectedLang && rawText.indexOf('\n') === -1 && rawText.indexOf(': ') === -1) return;

      var parent = code.parentNode;
      var target = parent.tagName === 'P' && parent.children.length === 1 ? parent : code;
      target.parentNode.replaceChild(wrapper, target);
      var codeEl = wrapper.querySelector('code');
      hljs.highlightElement(codeEl);

      var lines = splitHtmlLines(codeEl.innerHTML);
      if (lines[lines.length - 1] === '') lines.pop();
      codeEl.innerHTML = lines
        .map(function (l) {

        navigator.clipboard.writeText(rawText).then(function () {

          setTimeout(function () {

        });
      });

      wrapper.querySelector('.code-expand-btn').addEventListener('click', function () {
        overlayBody.innerHTML = '<div class="code-content" style="padding:0 20px;">' + '<pre style="margin:0;background:transparent;padding:0;">' + '<code class="language-' + lang + ' hljs" style="font-size:13.5px;line-height:0.3;font-family:monospace;background:transparent;white-space:pre;display:block;counter-reset:line;"></code>' + '</pre>' + '</div>';

        overlay.classList.add('active');
      });
    });
  });

document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  if (window.matchMedia("(max-width: 767px)").matches) return;

  const images = document.querySelectorAll(".blog-post-content figure.w-richtext-figure-type-image img");

  images.forEach(function (img) {

    img.addEventListener("click", function () {
      const overlay = document.createElement("div");
      overlay.style.position = "fixed";
      overlay.style.inset = "0";
      overlay.style.zIndex = "9999";
      overlay.style.background = "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.86)";
      overlay.style.display = "flex";
      overlay.style.alignItems = "center";
      overlay.style.justifyContent = "center";
      overlay.style.padding = "32px";
      overlay.style.cursor = "zoom-out";
      overlay.style.opacity = "0";
      overlay.style.transition = "opacity 220ms ease";

      const fullImage = document.createElement("img");
      fullImage.src = img.currentSrc || img.src;
      fullImage.alt = img.alt || "";
      fullImage.style.maxWidth = "100%";
      fullImage.style.maxHeight = "100%";
      fullImage.style.objectFit = "contain";
      fullImage.style.transform = "scale(0.96)";
      fullImage.style.transition = "transform 220ms ease";

      overlay.appendChild(fullImage);
      document.body.appendChild(overlay);
      document.body.style.overflow = "hidden";

      requestAnimationFrame(function () {
        overlay.style.opacity = "1";
        fullImage.style.transform = "scale(1)";
      });

      function close() {
        overlay.style.opacity = "0";
        fullImage.style.transform = "scale(0.96)";

        setTimeout(function () {
          overlay.remove();
          document.body.style.overflow = "";
          document.removeEventListener("keydown", onKeydown);
        }, 220);
      }

      function onKeydown(event) {
        if (event.key === "Escape") close();
      }

      overlay.addEventListener("click", close);
      document.addEventListener("keydown", onKeydown);
    });
  });
});
